utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, but they were from the previous authority bodies. Both Mr. Mirko Jovanovic and Milos Bogdanovic, and they were active on the previous authority bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: They were elected to the Executive Council of the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo under formation; isn't that true? Isn't that correct, according to this document?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. But as I've said before, they were on the former government. They headed the Executive Board or the department, respectively.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you'll further notice that Lazar Mirkic was not named head of economic affairs at the Pik factory --

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirkic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: -- Mirkic. But in fact had been elected secretary of municipal secretariat for the economy back in March 28th of 1992, weeks before, three weeks before the -- or almost three weeks before the Pik meeting; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. He was elected at the meeting. But the Assembly was not functioning, nor was it meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that's because it was some sort of shadow or parallel government, isn't that correct, sir, because there was an elected government currently in office?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And further, we notice that Mico Ivanovic was elected commander of the Territorial Defence, municipal staff, and Stevan Todorovic was named chief of the public security station, both in Bosanski Samac; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's -- if I may just add, was the choice of Mr. Todorovic. I watched scenes. At first, he was not foreseen. It was Stevo Peric. However, he exerted enormous pressure on Mr. Ilija Ristic and the others, and he lobbied for himself as the only possible candidate for the president, that is, the chief of the MUP. I think they tried to harmonise the whole thing, but there was pressure, and then he was finally elected.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So 11 members of the Executive Council of that assembly were elected at that meeting; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And in addition to that, if you continue on, the assembly charges the new Executive Council president and senior officials to organise the work of the organs of administration and to carry out preparations, transition to work under wartime. Do you see that in Article 2?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So they were establishing the administrative bodies of a government. They were giving orders to start the establishment of the administrative bodies of a government which was developing; isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are decisions by the assembly, as far as I know, and I was not an active member, nor did I speak at that meeting. I was merely a spectator, and I couldn't know. This is actually the first time I get to see the wording of that particular decision. These organs, as far as I know, never met, and it's obvious that what you've just shown me, that the Crisis Staff, including those officials, or rather, officials -- but you can see who was elected to the Crisis Staff, and that is not consistent with the previous decision. I was not familiarised with that particular decision. I said what I know, and I told you about what I actually participated in.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you agree that Blagoje Simic, the president of the municipal chapter of the SDS party, was appointed president of the Crisis Staff of the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac, and that was done at the initiative of the SDS party? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't speak about an SDS initiative, because I was not a member of the SDS and I didn't take part in the work of their organs. Whether they proposed Blagoje as the president of the SDS to also be the president, if you look at the wording of the decision on the setting up of crisis staffs, the document you've shown me, there's something I don't seem to understand. Who were supposed to be the members? This man or that man. So this comment, as for myself, I'm not sure I can give a comment on that, because I was not a member of the party. Whether someone else was supposed to be appointed president of the assembly, perhaps, and then yet another person the president of the Crisis Staff. I do have the feeling as for what was going on, that all those who were named in the different sectors were sort of avoiding becoming members of that body, and I told you already that one of those people asked me what I was doing in the Crisis Staff, and then you interrupted me, which means -- well, you see what it was like, how it went, and how the body was set up. You see that the people who were eventually nominated and who became members -- later, Miroslav Tadic, because he was the head of civilian protection, was pushed into the Crisis Staff, not of his own free will, but someone made him, someone told him: Come on, Miro. And then another person who was elected a member of the Crisis Staff and wasn't present was Simeon Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Simeon Simic, the defendant Blagoje Simic's cousin we're talking about, correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've mentioned his name. He was also made to become a member of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the defendant Blagoje Simic's other cousin was Milan Simic, who was president of the Executive Board; isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but in yesterday's testimony, or perhaps it was this morning, the president of the Executive Board, the president at that time, Mr. Jovanovic, who, by this decision of the Serbian municipality of Samac, was re-elected, the president was removed, with the assistance of Mr. Todorovic, because he didn't like him. Then Mr. Milan Simic became the head of the Executive Council, because he was Mr. Todorovic's friend. They socialised. And he simply imposed his nomination on us, him as the head of that body.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, Milan Simic was related to Blagoje Simic and he was also related to Stevan Todorovic, isn't that correct, four people related?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I don't know about Stevan Todorovic. I know that he was married to his relative, but I didn't know that they were relatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. Let's continue on with Blagoje Simic. If you could look at the 14th of April, 1992, the conclusions of the Executive Council, please. In P124, this is page 21. There are six conclusions. Conclusion number 1, sir -- actually, can you see that, sir? Can you see it clearly? Sir, can you see that on your monitor in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If you look at number 1, we'll start off with, and these are the conclusions: "To take immediate steps to form the municipal Crisis Staff in accordance with the relevant assembly decision." And we've already gone through assembly decision. Do you see that? Did I read that correctly?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And let's look at number 5: "The Executive Council" --

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can see that. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: -- "considers that the conditions are not propitious for convening a session of the Municipal Assembly. The Executive Council supports the initiative of the Samac municipal board of the Serbian Democratic Party for Dr. Blagoje Simic to be elected president of the Municipal Assembly at the first session of that assembly." Did I read that correctly?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, perfectly correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And since that assembly did not meet until 1993, he was named president of the Crisis Staff; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And I'd also like you to look at Article 3. The assign -- or it says: "To assign to the chief of the public security station the task of immediately forming a special-purpose unit of MUP, Ministry of Internal Affairs, attached to the SJB, public security station, in collaboration with the responsible bodies of the military and civilian authorities." Did I read that correctly?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So that conclusion or that assignment that's been given to Stevan Todorovic, the police chief, is to establish a special-purpose unit, a police unit, isn't that correct, that's going to collaborate with the bodies of the -- the responsible bodies of the military and civilian authorities?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's what the conclusion says, but that's not how it actually was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And I want to just continue on to the next set of conclusions, which are the last. From the 15th of April, 1992. And would you look at conclusion number 3, dated April 15th, 1992: "The special-purpose unit attached to the SJB, the public security station, in collaboration with the Serbian Territorial Defence, shall immediately take steps and measures, with a view to protecting the Serbian people in Bosanski Samac and other parts of the Posavina against another genocide." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown 164 ter, P164 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, the document in front of you is the factual basis for plea of guilt of Biljana Plavsic, who we were talking about, the former president of the SDA and the former member of the presidency of the Republic of Srpska. In paragraph 12, can you see it in front of you on the monitor, sir?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try and read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Why don't I read it and you just follow along, sir: " In addition, the SDS prepared and distributed written instructions to SDS municipal leaders to form crisis staffs, proclaim Serbian municipal assemblies, carry out the preparations for the formation of municipal government bodies, and to mobilise the Serb police and Territorial Defence forces and subordinate them to the JNA command. The municipal crisis staffs implemented these objectives and directives in the field, including ultimately the objective of ethnic separation by force."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Maybe -- it's not objection; it's just a suggestion. Maybe it's a slip of the tongue of my learned friend. In fact, when he made a citation, he said "Serb police." But in paragraph 12 of plea agreement, which is not a judgement, just a plea agreement, said: "Bosnian Serb police." So we have to be cautious about that, to be precise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'll read it again. That's no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: "In addition, the SDS prepared and distributed written instructions to SDS municipal leaders to form crisis staffs, proclaim Serbian assemblies, and carry out preparations for the formation of municipal government bodies and to mobilise Bosnian Serb police and Territorial Defence forces and to subordinate them to the JNA command. The municipal crisis staffs implemented these objectives and directives in the field, including ultimately the objective of ethnic separation by force." Did I read that correctly, sir?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. But the second part, the conclusion, this was implemented. We know that. But I don't think it was included in the original [indiscernible], because this is merely a comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But you agree with me, sir, that the -- what we've been just talking about, the establishment of the Crisis Staff, the Serbian municipality, the Serb police, Territorial Defence leader, all of those things, just as Mrs. Plavsic indicated, all occurred in Bosanski Samac? You agree with that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday, and today, I said that while I was following what was going on in politics in Bosnia and Herzegovina and in Samac, I attended both sessions of the both assemblies, and now the conclusions of the Executive Council that you've shown me and the meeting, I don't know whether it was held or not. I can't say that there was indeed such a meeting of the Executive Council and that any such directive was issued and that the chief of the MUP which should do this or that specifically. As for Biljana Plavsic, this was going down the SDS line. I was not a member, and I was not a member of any of the organs of the SDS. I simply didn't have access to that kind of information. I was not in a position to know what the president of the SDS had been ordered to do. But I know that even in the SDS, as far as Samac municipality was concerned, the situation was not really particularly favourable. There were three factions inside the party itself, as far as I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, that's not my question. These things which Biljana Plavsic says that the SDS instructed the municipal leaders to do, didn't these things happen in Samac? Let's take them one by one. You've already testified to them. A Crisis Staff was formed or established; isn't that true, sir?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it was established, but at the beginning it wasn't functioning according to these instructions --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, the question, please --

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Nor was it set up the way it had been ordered to be set up.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The question -- it says here that they are to form a Crisis Staff, and my question to you is: Was a Crisis Staff formed? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, it was set up.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Number 2: "Proclaim Serbian municipal assemblies. The Serbian municipal assembly of Samac and Pelagicevo under formation was established and proclaimed."

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's indisputable.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Next, number 3: "Carry out preparations for the formation of municipal government bodies." You testified that you were present when 11 members of the Executive Council were elected and that they were ordered, as the rest of that directive, to start establishing and putting together their government. So weren't preparations for the formation of municipal bodies, where the SDS instructed to carry out preparation ares for the formation of muncipal government bodies, that occurred. You were there for that.

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was there, but these documents -- I see them now for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It further says: "To mobilise Bosnian Serb police." You saw -- or you were present for the election of Stevan Todorovic, and you saw those orders for him to establish a police unit. You saw that in the documents that we just went through, document P124, the Official Gazette of the municipality of Samac. Do you agree that there was an order to mobilise the Bosnian Serb police and, in addition, Stevan Todorovic was named police chief of this so-called shadow or parallel Serb government?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stevan Todorovic had manipulated people; and yes, he was appointed chief. But this is the first time I actually see this decision, the way it was worded. And as far as I can see, it dates back to July, but the documents themselves were actually drafted later. So at the time when the assembly session and the Executive Board meeting were held, no one will be able to convince me that this was written at that time. Probably when lawyers were appointed, the wording itself came later. I see these documents now for the first time in my life, and no one ever informed me of the existence of any such documents, nor did the Crisis Staff ever discuss these decisions or documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, my question to you is: Was Stevan Todorovic elected police chief, and was he also ordered by the assembly to start to put together a special police unit? You've read that. Do you agree that that happened?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was appointed. But at the session, no one explicitly ordered him what to do, nor were there any conclusions like that. I had no occasion to judge that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Those were at two later sessions in April, which you weren't present for the April 14th and 15th sessions, were you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, because there is a confusing question from the part of my learned friend. He's speaking about two later sessions in April, namely, on April 14th and 15th, and does that relate to Executive Board session or assembly session? Because in previous question, he asked him -- my learned friend asked the witness, in page 99, line 6: And he was also ordered by the assembly to start to put together special police unit. So it's a bit confusing issue here. Which session do you mean: Executive Board or assembly? Simple as that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness isn't confused. He's read and he's followed along right from the Official Gazette. He knows which sessions we're talking about. Was he present or was he not present. If the Court would like to break now and we can go on with this tomorrow, we can happily do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We've come to the end of our session today.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I just have one brief moment to raise one issue with the Trial Chamber before we break. It is related to our witness, Mr. Mirko Pavic. I spoke to Mr. Pistoljevic yesterday in the afternoon and I would like to inform the Trial Chamber that Mr. Pavic won't be able to attend videolink testimony. His health condition is not good enough to come to Belgrade and testify, if such a decision would be made by the Trial Chamber, not at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. But we have another witness, Mustafa Pistoljevic, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the statement of this witness that I already tendered into evidence. I already offered it. We have a number for it, so Your Honours could make a decision about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, also before we break, this witness indicated that he had some sort of problem for being here tomorrow. Has that been taken care of? Has that been resolved? Is he available for all day tomorrow? Because apparently they're going to have to move Mr. Pistoljevic in between to get him on and off quickly. His wife is very ill.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It depends on your schedule, my learned friend, how long you're going to keep this witness in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: He can --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What's your estimation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: He can appear tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Maybe he can answer -- he can answer himself. I do believe that there is a session at noon in Republika Srpska, so I don't know if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. -- let me ask him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If one hour and a half would be enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, you are required -- yes. You are required to appear tomorrow morning to continue cross-examination, so that we can complete your evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I could, but I must attend at 12.00 in Bijeljina, because the meeting of the Executive Board of the football association cannot go ahead without me, because I am the administrator for several key issues. And I may make it in one hour, perhaps one hour and a half. I need at least that amount of time to reach Bijeljina. I've informed the Defence team that I had the meeting on another day, but then the meeting was rescheduled for Friday so that I could make it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's going very slowly. I thought we would be a little bit farther ahead. I'll probably need him at least another few hours, at least. He was, as the Court knows, a member of the Crisis Staff, the War Presidency, he was the head of the military civilian council in Odzak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So we should continue with him on Monday?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That would be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Savo Popovic, so we'll be able to continue with you on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I haven't got an answer from the witness. I'm waiting for an answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's acceptable. Monday sounds good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well, then.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I could come back on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well, then. Monday, 9.00, we'll start with you, so tomorrow you can go and attend your meeting. Thank you. So we'll see you on Monday, Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just a brief remark about my witness, but can we go into private session, please, for this?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, do I understand well that tomorrow Mr. Popovic will be one hour and a half --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no, no. He won't come tomorrow. He's coming on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I see. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I merely wanted to say the following -- are we in private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Are we in private session? Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: 1.57 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 7th day of March 2003, at 10.30 a.m.
